generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Sample from a pool of 8-20 distinct short strings; 5% of rows get a near-variant (case change, trailing space, or one-character edit) of a pool value; nullable columns get NULL in 5-15% of rows.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Sample from a pool of 40-80 distinct surname-like and 40-80 given-name-like strings; 10% near-variants (case change or one-character edit); nullable columns get NULL in 5-15% of rows.
generic_sampling_rules.text_code: Sample from a pool of 8-12 distinct 3-letter uppercase codes; 10% near-variants (case change or one-character edit); nullable columns get NULL in 5-15% of rows, except primary-key codes which are drawn from a fresh, non-colliding pool (see dependencies and uncertainty).
generic_sampling_rules.integer_small: Sample uniformly from the observed distinct values; include the minimum and maximum; nullable columns get NULL in 5-15% of rows.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_price: Sample integers from the observed range with step 25; include the minimum and maximum; nullable columns get NULL in 5-15% of rows.
generic_sampling_rules.real_rate: Sample from the observed distinct values with step 6.25; include the minimum and maximum; nullable columns get NULL in 5-15% of rows.
generic_sampling_rules.date_text: Sample a date in DD-MON-YY format between 01-JAN-10 and 31-DEC-11; nullable columns get NULL in 5-15% of rows.
generic_sampling_rules.primary_key_integer: Assign sequential integers starting at max(compact Reservations.Code) + 1 (a per-instance margin of +1 is sufficient because each instance is a separate copy of the compact DB); never NULL and never colliding with compact rows.
generic_sampling_rules.primary_key_text: Assign values drawn from a fresh pool of 3-letter uppercase codes disjoint from the compact Rooms.RoomId values; number of generated Rooms rows is 10 and the values are 10 distinct fresh codes; never NULL and never colliding with compact rows.

targets.duplicate_share: measured over distinct parent values referenced (not over child rows): with 10 parent rows and 600 child rows, distinct/n is at most 10/600 = 1.7%; the target is interpreted as distinct referenced parent values / child rows, i.e. all 10 parent values are referenced and at least 9 of them are referenced by the generated child rows

uncertainty.Primary-key collisions with compact rows: The compact DB already contains Rooms.RoomId values from the shared 3-letter code pool and Reservations.Code values 10105, 10183, 10449, 10489, 10500, 10574, 10984, 10990. Generated primary keys must be disjoint: Rooms.RoomId from a fresh 10-code pool disjoint from compact RoomIds; Reservations.Code sequential starting at max(compact Code)+1 per instance. This guarantees table_sizes_per_instance (Rooms 10, Reservations 600) are actually added.
uncertainty.NOT NULL vs planted NULLs: Compact null_rate is 0.0 for every column, but null_targets contains Reservations.Room (nullable FK, 5% NULL) and Rooms.bedType (5-30% NULL) because the atomic-operation summary requires NULL rows for those columns. All other columns (Rooms.basePrice, Reservations.Rate, FirstName, LastName, CheckIn, CheckOut, etc.) are NOT NULL and never receive NULL. The instruction-7 'at least one NULL row per nullable column' clause is satisfied only for the columns in null_targets; all other nullable columns are generated with no NULLs because the compact share of 0 overrides the 'at least one NULL' clause for them. Planted NULLs are never replaced.
uncertainty.Reservations.Rate vs Rooms.basePrice: No universal formula is stated: sample most Rate values from the real_rate domain (step 6.25 including min/max). On a controlled subset of rows (at least 3 per instance, deterministically cycling through offsets -1, 0, +1) plant Rate such that Rate - basePrice of the reservation's Room equals -1, 0, or 1, so the join-level expression takes the boundary values while the general Rate domain is preserved. Rate must be looked up relative to the actual referenced Room.
uncertainty.Reservations.Room group sizes and duplic: Construct Reservations.Room explicitly: draw wins over the 10 fresh RoomIds with a controlled multiplicity distribution so at least one group has size 1, at least one has size 2, at least one has size >= 3, and the number of distinct referenced parent values is at least 9 (the 10th parent room is referenced by no child rows, so the parent-without-children target holds). The duplicate_share target is measured over distinct parent values referenced, not over child rows, because with 10 parent rows and 600 child rows the maximum distinct/n is 10/600 = 1.7%. Plant ~5% NULL FKs. The count vector must be initialized to length k before filling the distribution so that the loop never indexes out of range.
uncertainty.Tie targets for Rooms.decor and Rooms.ro: Force exact count distributions: Rooms.decor counts (4, 3, 3) across 10 rows and Rooms.roomName counts (4, 3, 3), so the minimum count is tied at rank 1 for COUNT(decor) ASC and guaranteed ties at rank 1 for ORDER BY COUNT(roomName) ASC. Rooms.roomName is restricted to 3 distinct values to satisfy group_sizes (1, 2, >= 3 partition, e.g. 4/3/3) and duplicates_for_distinct (20-50%), overriding generic text_short; no NULL for roomName.
uncertainty.Writer preserves compact rows: The generation program must pass the original database path to write_instance_sqlite (orig_path=orig); generated rows are appended and compact rows are never deleted or altered.
uncertainty.Rooms.RoomId duplicates/group_sizes for: RoomId is a primary key and cannot contain duplicates; the duplicates_for_distinct and group_sizes entries in the atomic summary for Rooms.RoomId describe join-visible multiplicities through Reservations.Room, not duplicate PK values.
uncertainty.Rooms.basePrice observed range: The observed range is derived from the compact data (schema.original_values[('Rooms','basePrice')]) rather than hardcoded; the integer_price domain samples with step 25 over that range and includes the minimum and maximum. The planted boundary values 140/141/142/159/160/161 fall inside the observed range and are on top of the general domain.
